[[File:Leo Zippin.jpeg|thumb|Leo Zippin]]

'''Leo Zippin''' (January 25, 1905 – May 11, 1995) was an American mathematician.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=NY Times|date=May 20, 1995|title=Leo Zippin, 90, Dies; Solved Math Puzzle|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/05/20/obituaries/leo-zippin-90-dies-solved-math-puzzle.html}}</ref>  He is best known for solving [[Hilbert's fifth problem|Hilbert's Fifth Problem]] with [[Deane Montgomery]] and [[Andrew M. Gleason]] in 1952.

==Biography==
Leo Zippin was born in 1905 to Bella Salwen and Max Zippin, who had emigrated to New York City from [[Ukraine]] in 1903. He did his [[undergraduate]] and [[Graduate degree|graduate]] work at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1929. His doctoral adviser was [[John Robert Kline]].

Leo Zippin is the author of ''The Uses Of Infinity'', and together with Deane Montgomery, the monograph ''Topological Transformation Groups''. In 1952, he, along with [[Andrew M. Gleason]] and [[Deane Montgomery]] solved [[Hilbert's fifth problem]].<ref name="EarmanGlymour1977">{{cite book |last=Stein |first=Howard |editor-last1=Earman |editor-first1=John |editor-link=John Earman |editor-last2=Glymour |editor-first2=Clark N. |editor2-link=Clark Glymour |editor-last3=Stachel |editor-first3=John J. |editor3-link=John Stachel |title=Foundations of space-time theories |chapter=Some Philosophical Prehistory of General Relativity |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iorglDZWVcwC&pg=PA38 |accessdate=22 May 2011|year=1977|publisher=U of Minnesota Press|isbn=978-0-8166-0807-2|pages=38–}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Montgomery, Deane|author2=Zippin, Leo|title=Small subgroups of finite-dimensional groups|journal=Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A|date=May 1952|volume=38|issue=5|pages=440–442|pmc=1063582|doi=10.1073/pnas.38.5.440|pmid=16589121|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He married Frances Levinson in 1932.  They had two children, [[Nina Baym|Nina]], a prominent literary critic and literary historian, and Vivian.<ref>[http://www.gkh.com/attorney-profiles/vivian-b-narehood/ known as Vivian B. Narehood, an attorney at Gibbel Kraybill & Hess] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131205003617/http://www.gkh.com/attorney-profiles/vivian-b-narehood/ |date=2013-12-05 }}</ref>  He taught at [[Queens College]] in [[Flushing, NY]].
